claim: Tumor immunology is undergoing a renaissance due to the recent profound clinical successes of tumor immunotherapy.
source: Tumor immunology is undergoing a renaissance due to the recent profound clinical successes of tumor immunotherapy.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field's current state, supported by the context of recent clinical advances in immunotherapy.

claim: Systems Biology became well established around 2000.
source: While the discipline of systems biology became well established around 2000 (Ideker et al., 2001), its underlying concepts have been appreciated for over half a century (Waterman and Theory, 1968; Kitano, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ideker et al., 2001.

claim: The underlying concepts of systems biology have been appreciated for over half a century.
source: While the discipline of systems biology became well established around 2000 (Ideker et al., 2001), its underlying concepts have been appreciated for over half a century (Waterman and Theory, 1968; Kitano, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Waterman and Theory, 1968 and Kitano, 2002.

claim: The study of medicine represents an original implementation of Systems Biology.
source: Indeed, some have suggested that the study of medicine, which requires an understanding of the complex interactions between multiple molecules, cell types, and organ systems in response to different treatments over time, represents an original implementation of Systems Biology (Germain, 2018).
evidence: The claim is attributed to Germain, 2018.

claim: Animal models are frequently imperfect surrogates for human biology.
source: Nonetheless, animal models are frequently imperfect surrogates for human biology.
evidence: This is a general statement about the limitations of animal models, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: There are many instances where there exists a stark divergence in phenotypes for orthologs of different species.
source: While orthologous genes typically elicit similar functions across species, there are many instances where there exists a stark divergence in phenotypes for orthologs of different species (Gharib and Robinson-Rechavi, 2011; Koonin, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gharib and Robinson-Rechavi, 2011 and Koonin, 2005.

claim: Inhibitory signaling in natural killer (NK) cells following recognition of major histocompatibility (MHC) class Ia molecules is achieved by Ly49 family members in mice but killer immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIRs) in humans.
source: For example, inhibitory signaling in natural killer (NK) cells following recognition of major histocompatibility (MHC) class Ia molecules is achieved by Ly49 family members in mice but killer immunoglobulin-like receptors (KIRs) in humans (Lanier, 2005; Karlhofer et al., 1992; Moretta et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lanier, 2005; Karlhofer et al., 1992; and Moretta et al., 1990.

claim: Only 8% of drugs entering clinical trials succeed in Phase I.
source: Even with improved animal models, however, there are many instances where they fail to predict clinical responses, and only 8% of drugs entering clinical trials succeed in Phase I (Mak et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mak et al., 2014.

claim: Mathematical models have been used to track the development of resistance in CML.
source: For example, such models have tracked the development of resistance in CML (Michor et al., 2005) or have served as the basis for clinical trials altering dosing strategies (Norton and Simon, 1977; Citron et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Michor et al., 2005.

claim: Adaptive therapy using an evolutionary game theory model extended the time to progression in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer.
source: In an approach they term 'adaptive therapy', one group used an evolutionary game theory model to predict patient-specific treatment responses in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer, modifying their treatment accordingly, and in doing so, extended the time to progression in these patients (Zhang et al., 2017a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2017a.

claim: The beginning of modern-era systems biology largely coincides with the Human Genome Project.
source: Indeed, the beginning of modern-era systems biology largely coincides with the Human Genome Project (Lander et al., 2001; Venter et al., 2001; International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium, 2004), which enabled researchers to interrogate the genome-wide contributions of mutations to diseases.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lander et al., 2001; Venter et al., 2001; and International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium, 2004.

claim: Cancer is a genetic disease at its core.
source: At its core, cancer is a genetic disease; malignant transformation is the consequence of mutations in tumor suppressor genes and oncogenes (Stratton et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stratton et al., 2009.

claim: The genomic loci for BCR and TCR undergo rearrangement to generate diversity of the antigen-recognition domains.
source: The genomic loci for these receptors undergo rearrangement in order to generate diversity of the antigen-recognition domains in a manner that confers specific immunity against an enormous range of pathogens (Hozumi and Tonegawa, 1976).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hozumi and Tonegawa, 1976.

claim: Methylation represents one of the most common epigenetic modifications for silencing transcription.
source: Methylation represents one of the most common epigenetic modifications for silencing transcription (Jones and Takai, 2001), and can be surveyed at the genome level through the use of Whole Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) or Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS), which use sodium bisulfite to convert unmethylated cytosine residues to uracil while leaving their methylated counterparts (5-methylcytosine) intact (Frommer et al., 1992; Lister et al., 2009; Meissner et al., 2005; Booth et al., 2012; Booth et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jones and Takai, 2001.

claim: ChIP-seq has been used to define the super-enhancer (SE) landscape in CD4+ T cells and identify how polymorphisms in these regions can potentiate risk of autoimmune disease.
source: For example, ChIP-seq has been used to define the super-enhancer (SE) landscape in CD4+ T cells and identify how polymorphisms in these regions can potentiate risk of autoimmune disease (Vahedi et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vahedi et al., 2015.

claim: ChIP-seq has uncovered the regulatory epigenetic signatures that distinguish the naïve, effector, central memory, and effector memory CD8+ T cell subsets.
source: Similarly, using ChIP-seq to profile a variety of methylation and acetylation patterns of Histone H3, researchers have uncovered the regulatory epigenetic signatures that distinguish the naïve, effector, central memory, and effector memory CD8+ T cell subsets (He et al., 2016; Rodriguez et al., 2017; Araki et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to He et al., 2016; Rodriguez et al., 2017; and Araki et al., 2009.

claim: Long-range distal elements, such as enhancers, affect gene expression even at distances greater than 1 Mb in linear genome space.
source: While regions of open chromatin reveal evidence of transcriptional regulation, higher order chromatin structures also play critical roles in controlling gene expression. Long-range distal elements, such as enhancers, affect gene expression even at distances greater than 1 Mb in linear genome space (Lettice et al., 2003; Bulger and Groudine, 2011; Dekker, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lettice et al., 2003; Bulger and Groudine, 2011; and Dekker, 2008.

claim: Flow cytometry served as the primary means for identifying individuals at risk for AIDS and monitoring their course and response to therapy, based on the relative frequency of circulating CD4 T cells, prior to the discovery of HIV.
source: For example, prior to the discovery of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus, it served as the primary means for identifying individuals at risk for AIDS and monitoring their course and response to therapy, based on the relative frequency of circulating CD4 T cells (Lifson and Engleman, 1989).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lifson and Engleman, 1989.

claim: Mass cytometry enables researchers to measure the expression of more than 40 proteins simultaneously on single cells.
source: One of the most widely adopted technologies used by systems immunologists is mass cytometry (CyTOF) (Bendall et al., 2012). This approach replaces fluorescent tags on antibodies with transition element metal isotopes, to enable measurement of single cells labeled with such antibodies using time-of-flight mass spectrometry (Bandura et al., 2009; Bendall et al., 2011). This technology enables researchers to measure the expression of more than 40 proteins simultaneously on single cells, by eliminating limitations derived from spectral overlap of fluorescent probes.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bendall et al., 2012; Bandura et al., 2009; and Bendall et al., 2011.

claim: Tumors often acquire tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), which closely resemble lymphoid follicles.
source: Tumors often acquire tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), which closely resemble lymphoid follicles, containing T cells, B cells, FDCs, Tfh-like cells, fibroblast reticular cells (FRCs), and even high endothial venules (HEVs) (Jones et al., 2016; Goc et al., 2013; Dieu-Nosjean et al., 2014; Colbeck et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jones et al., 2016; Goc et al., 2013; Dieu-Nosjean et al., 2014; and Colbeck et al., 2017.

claim: The presence of TLSs in tumors has classically correlated with improved survival in a variety of cancers.
source: Although TLSs can serve as a source of protumoral Tregs (Joshi et al., 2015), their presence in tumors has classically correlated with improved survival in a variety of cancers (Colbeck et al., 2017; Ladányi et al., 2007; Dieu-Nosjean et al., 2008; Pitzalis et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Colbeck et al., 2017; Ladányi et al., 2007; Dieu-Nosjean et al., 2008; and Pitzalis et al., 2014.

claim: Rudolf Virchow first recognized that tumors frequently contain leukocytes in the mid-nineteenth century.
source: In the mid-nineteenth century, Rudolf Virchow first recognized that tumors frequently contain leukocytes. He posited that chronic inflammation lies at the origins of tumors (Virchow, 1863; Virchow, 1858), leading Dvorak, 1986, to describe tumors as 'wounds that do not heal', a century later.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Virchow, 1863 and Virchow, 1858.

claim: Dvorak described tumors as 'wounds that do not heal'.
source: In the mid-nineteenth century, Rudolf Virchow first recognized that tumors frequently contain leukocytes. He posited that chronic inflammation lies at the origins of tumors (Virchow, 1863; Virchow, 1858), leading Dvorak, 1986, to describe tumors as 'wounds that do not heal', a century later.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dvorak, 1986.

claim: Macrophages within tissues are derived from either circulating bone-marrow-derived monocytes or from macrophages seeded during development.
source: Macrophages within tissues are derived from one of two sources: either, they differentiate from circulating bone-marrow-derived monocytes that have extravasated from blood vessels or, in the case of some specialized tissues, they were seeded during development by macrophages derived from the yolk sac or monocytes from the fetal liver (Ginhoux and Guilliams, 2016; Epelman et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ginhoux and Guilliams, 2016 and Epelman et al., 2014.

claim: Langerhans cells of the epidermis are tissue-resident macrophages derived from yolk sac or fetal liver monocytes.
source: Langerhans cells of the epidermis (Merad et al., 2002), microglia of the brain (Ginhoux et al., 2010; Ajami et al., 2007; Yona et al., 2013), Kupffer cells of the liver (Yona et al., 2013), and alveolar macrophages of the lungs (Yona et al., 2013; Hashimoto et al., 2013; Guilliams et al., 2013) are all examples of the latter ontogeny and are known as tissue-resident macrophages.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Merad et al., 2002.

claim: Microglia of the brain are tissue-resident macrophages derived from yolk sac or fetal liver monocytes.
source: Langerhans cells of the epidermis (Merad et al., 2002), microglia of the brain (Ginhoux et al., 2010; Ajami et al., 2007; Yona et al., 2013), Kupffer cells of the liver (Yona et al., 2013), and alveolar macrophages of the lungs (Yona et al., 2013; Hashimoto et al., 2013; Guilliams et al., 2013) are all examples of the latter ontogeny and are known as tissue-resident macrophages.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ginhoux et al., 2010; Ajami et al., 2007; and Yona et al., 2013.

claim: Kupffer cells of the liver are tissue-resident macrophages derived from yolk sac or fetal liver monocytes.
source: Langerhans cells of the epidermis (Merad et al., 2002), microglia of the brain (Ginhoux et al., 2010; Ajami et al., 2007; Yona et al., 2013), Kupffer cells of the liver (Yona et al., 2013), and alveolar macrophages of the lungs (Yona et al., 2013; Hashimoto et al., 2013; Guilliams et al., 2013) are all examples of the latter ontogeny and are known as tissue-resident macrophages.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yona et al., 2013.

claim: Alveolar macrophages of the lungs are tissue-resident macrophages derived from yolk sac or fetal liver monocytes.
source: Langerhans cells of the epidermis (Merad et al., 2002), microglia of the brain (Ginhoux et al., 2010; Ajami et al., 2007; Yona et al., 2013), Kupffer cells of the liver (Yona et al., 2013), and alveolar macrophages of the lungs (Yona et al., 2013; Hashimoto et al., 2013; Guilliams et al., 2013) are all examples of the latter ontogeny and are known as tissue-resident macrophages.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yona et al., 2013; Hashimoto et al., 2013; and Guilliams et al., 2013.

claim: M1 macrophages exhibit elevated MHC-II expression and produce nitrous oxide (NO), reactive oxygen species (ROS), TNF-α, and a milieu of inflammatory cytokines.
source: M1 macrophages (or classically activated macrophages) were thought to represent a state of polarization induced by Th1-derived cytokines such as IFN-γ or microbial stimuli (e.g. LPS). They exhibit elevated MHC-II expression and produce nitrous oxide (NO), reactive oxygen species (ROS), TNF-α, and a milieu of inflammatory cytokines (e.g. IL-12, IL-23, IL-6, IL-1, etc.) (Dalton et al., 1993; Mantovani et al., 2004; Atri et al., 1801).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dalton et al., 1993; Mantovani et al., 2004; and Atri et al., 1801.

claim: M2 macrophages express arginase 1, IL-10, CCL17, CCL22, and CCL24 and are generally considered anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive.
source: In contrast, M2 macrophages (alternatively-activated macrophages) were initially reported to be polarized by Th2 cytokines such as IL-4 and IL-13 that drive alternative macrophage activation (Stein et al., 1992; Doyle et al., 1994; Gordon, 2003). These macrophages express arginase 1, IL-10, CCL17, CCL22, and CCL24 and are generally considered anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive (Biswas and Mantovani, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Biswas and Mantovani, 2010.

claim: The binary interpretation of macrophage polarization as M1/M2 is vastly oversimplified and fails to capture the diversity of phenotypes exhibited by macrophages.
source: Recently, a number of studies that have employed systems approaches have revealed that this binary interpretation of macrophage polarization is vastly oversimplified and fails to capture the diversity of phenotypes exhibited by macrophages (Mosser and Edwards, 2008; Xue et al., 2014; Murray et al., 2014; Martinez and Gordon, 2014; Lavin et al., 2014; Ginhoux et al., 2016; Reinartz et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mosser and Edwards, 2008; Xue et al., 2014; Murray et al., 2014; Martinez and Gordon, 2014; Lavin et al., 2014; Ginhoux et al., 2016; Reinartz et al., 2014; and Zhang et al., 2019.

claim: Mass cytometry characterized 17 distinct TAM phenotypes in 73 clear cell renal cell carcinoma patients.
source: In one study that used mass cytometry to profile macrophages and T cells within the tumors of 73 clear cell renal cell carcinoma patients, the authors characterized 17 distinct TAM phenotypes (Chevrier et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chevrier et al., 2017.

claim: In human breast tumors, three TAM populations often expressed both M1 and M2 gene signatures in the same cells.
source: In particular, they noted considerable diversity in the myeloid compartments, and surprisingly, found a strong positive correlation between M1 and M2 gene signatures (Figure 3). The three TAM populations that they identified often expressed both gene signatures in the same cells, again suggesting that the original M1/M2 polarization concept does not recapitulate what occurs in vivo, particularly in human tumors.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from scRNA-seq analysis of breast tumors and is referenced in Figure 3.

claim: TAMs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma are derived from both blood monocytes and tissue-resident macrophages and these populations serve distinct functions during tumor progression.
source: A recent study that used parabiosis and congenic mice revealed that TAMs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma are derived from both blood monocytes and tissue-resident macrophages and that these populations serve distinct functions during tumor progression (Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhu et al., 2017.

claim: Both microglia and bone marrow-derived macrophages are involved in gliomas and exhibit distinct profiles and contributions to tumor progression.
source: Similarly, lineage-tracing approaches, scRNA-seq, and ATAC-seq have all been used to reveal that both microglia and bone marrow-derived macrophages are involved in gliomas and exhibit distinct profiles and contributions to tumor progression (Bowman et al., 2016; Müller et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bowman et al., 2016 and Müller et al., 2017.

claim: cDC1 express the chemokine receptor XCR1.
source: cDC1 express the chemokine receptor XCR1 (Bachem et al., 2012; Dorner et al., 2009), require the AP-1 transcription factor BATF3 for development (Hildner et al., 2008; Murphy et al., 2013), and are characterized by their ability to cross-present antigens to CD8+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bachem et al., 2012 and Dorner et al., 2009.

claim: cDC1 require the AP-1 transcription factor BATF3 for development.
source: cDC1 express the chemokine receptor XCR1 (Bachem et al., 2012; Dorner et al., 2009), require the AP-1 transcription factor BATF3 for development (Hildner et al., 2008; Murphy et al., 2013), and are characterized by their ability to cross-present antigens to CD8+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hildner et al., 2008 and Murphy et al., 2013.

claim: cDC1 are characterized by their ability to cross-present antigens to CD8+ T cells.
source: cDC1 express the chemokine receptor XCR1 (Bachem et al., 2012; Dorner et al., 2009), require the AP-1 transcription factor BATF3 for development (Hildner et al., 2008; Murphy et al., 2013), and are characterized by their ability to cross-present antigens to CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is a well-established characteristic of cDC1 cells in immunology.

claim: cDCs are critical for antitumor T-cell-mediated immunity.
source: cDCs are critical for antitumor T-cell-mediated immunity (Hildner et al., 2008; Fuertes et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hildner et al., 2008 and Fuertes et al., 2011.

claim: Migratory CD103+ peripheral cDC1s traffic to tumor-draining LNs in a CCR7-dependent fashion.
source: Furthermore, migratory CD103+ peripheral cDC1s traffic to tumor-draining LNs in a CCR7-dependent fashion, where they interact with tumor-specific T cells and transfer tumor antigens to other LN resident DC subsets, at much higher levels than migratory CD11b+ DCs (Roberts et al., 2016; Salmon et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Roberts et al., 2016 and Salmon et al., 2016.

claim: FcγR engagement of immune complexes (ICs) by DCs induces their CCR-7 dependent migration to LNs.
source: FcγR engagement of immune complexes (ICs) by DCs induces their CCR-7 dependent migration to LNs (Clatworthy et al., 2014), and we have shown that the combination of DC adjuvants with tumor-bound allogeneic antibody ICs induce robust anti-tumor T cell responses (Carmi et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Clatworthy et al., 2014.

claim: Flt3L injections vastly increase the numbers of CD103+ DCs in the TME.
source: One study, in which mass cytometry was used to evaluate the TME during early- and late-stage tumor development, showed that Flt3L injections vastly increases the numbers of CD103+ DCs in the TME (Salmon et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Salmon et al., 2016.

claim: Migration of cDC2s from tumors to the draining LNs is required for priming of CD4+ Tconv and eliciting a potent antitumor response.
source: Using scRNA-seq, one study found that migration of cDC2s from tumors to the draining LNs is required for priming of CD4+ Tconv and eliciting a potent antitumor response, but Tregs inhibit their efficacy likely by preventing their migration to the LNs (Figure 3; Binnewies et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Binnewies et al., 2019 and is referenced in Figure 3.

claim: T cell exhaustion was first identified in chronic viral infections.
source: T cell exhaustion, first identified in chronic viral infections (Zajac et al., 1998; Gallimore et al., 1998), is induced by persistent exposure to antigen accompanied by failure to eliminate it (Wherry, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zajac et al., 1998 and Gallimore et al., 1998.

claim: Features of exhaustion include elevated expression of inhibitory receptors, reduced cytokine expression, reduced proliferation, altered metabolism, and reduced effector function.
source: Features of exhaustion include elevated expression of inhibitory receptors (e.g. PD1, Lag3, Tim-3, etc.), reduced cytokine expression, reduced proliferation, altered metabolism, and reduced effector function (McLane et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McLane et al., 2019.

claim: The exhausted phenotype of tumor-specific T cells is regulated at an epigenetic level.
source: Through the use of systems approaches to evaluate the regulatory landscape of tumor-specific T cells, what has become abundantly clear is that, like most T cell states (Zhang et al., 2012; Shih et al., 2016; Yu et al., 2017), the exhausted phenotype of these cells is regulated at an epigenetic level, suggesting that TEx represent a distinct cell type (Figure 3; Sen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2012; Shih et al., 2016; Yu et al., 2017; and Sen et al., 2016, and is referenced in Figure 3.

claim: ATAC-seq revealed that naïve, effector, memory, and exhausted T cells exhibit profound differences in open chromatin regions (OCR).
source: Evaluation of chromatin accessibility landscapes by ATAC-seq has revealed that naïve, effector, memory, and exhausted T cells exhibit profound differences in open chromatin regions (OCR) (Sen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sen et al., 2016.

claim: PD-1 signaling blockade induces only moderate changes in the OCRs that do not revert the cells to a Tmem epigenetic profile.
source: While PD-1 signaling blockade can reinvigorate exhausted T cells, it induces only moderate changes in the OCRs that do not revert the cells to a Tmem epigenetic profile, perhaps explaining why the reinvigoration is transient (Pauken et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pauken et al., 2016.

claim: Combining DNA demethylating agents with PD-1 blockade has shown the potential to reverse the exhaustion state and improve antitumor response.
source: Yet while these epigenetic states persist during PD-1 blockade, as also evidenced through bisulfite sequencing, combining DNA demethylating agents with PD-1 blockade has shown the potential to reverse the exhaustion state and improve antitumor response (Ghoneim et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ghoneim et al., 2017.

claim: Epigenetic control of the exhaustion state is mediated by the transcription factor TOX.
source: Recent studies combining differential gene expression and OCR analyses between Tmem and TEx. suggest that epigenetic control of the exhaustion state is mediated by the transcription factor TOX, which is induced by chronic TCR stimulation, and in particular, calcineurin and NFAT signaling and is responsible for upregulation of inhibitory receptors such as PD1 (Khan et al., 2019; Alfei et al., 2019; Scott et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Khan et al., 2019; Alfei et al., 2019; and Scott et al., 2019.

claim: Genetic ablation of NR4A genes can prevent exhaustion in CAR-T cells and improve tumor clearance.
source: These effects extend to cell therapies, where genetic ablation of NR4A genes can prevent exhaustion in CAR-T cells and improve tumor clearance (Chen et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2019b.

claim: Progenitor TEx express high levels of TCF-1 or T-bet and exhibit the capacity to replenish the terminally differentiated TEx.
source: Progenitor TEx, or less-differentiated TEx, express high levels of TCF-1 or T-bet and exhibit the capacity to replenish the terminally differentiated TEx (Paley et al., 2012; Im et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2016; Utzschneider et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Paley et al., 2012; Im et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2016; and Utzschneider et al., 2016.

claim: ATAC-seq revealed distinct chromatin states that distinguish dysfunctional tumor-specific CD8+ T cells that can be recovered from those that are resistant to reprogramming.
source: As these states appear to be largely regulated at an epigenetic level, ATAC-seq has been used to reveal distinct chromatin states that distinguish dysfunctional tumor-specific CD8+ T cells that can be recovered from those that are resistant to reprogramming (Philip et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Philip et al., 2017.

claim: Droplet-based ATAC-seq revealed a massive expansion of TEx in patients post treatment with PD1 blockade.
source: A recent droplet-based ATAC-seq protocol that enables massively parallel scATAC-seq profiling was used to interrogate T cell exhaustion in tumors in the context of ICB (Satpathy et al., 2019). The results revealed a massive expansion of TEx in patients post treatment with PD1 blockade.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Satpathy et al., 2019.

claim: The transcriptional profile of T cells in melanoma forms a gradient of states exhibiting a range of profiles from highly cytotoxic to highly dysfunctional with shared clones occupying multiple transitional states of dysfunction.
source: A recent study that combined MARS-seq with single-cell TCR sequencing in melanoma patients to evaluate clonality of dysfunctional T cells revealed that the transcriptional profile of T cells forms a gradient of states exhibiting a range of profiles from highly cytotoxic to highly dysfunctional with shared clones occupying multiple transitional states of dysfunction (Li et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: The most proliferative T cells in melanoma tumors were the dysfunctional T cells.
source: Surprisingly, although TEx are thought to have a reduced proliferative capacity, the most proliferative T cells (by Ki67 and clonal expansion) were the dysfunctional T cells.
evidence: This is based on data from the study of melanoma T cells.

claim: T cells with transcriptional profiles analogous to resident memory T cells (TRM) can be found within breast cancer tumors and correlate with improved prognosis.
source: In breast cancer, researchers used scRNA-seq to reveal that T cells with transcriptional profiles analogous to resident memory T cells (TRM) can be found within tumors and correlate with improved prognosis (Savas et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Savas et al., 2018.

claim: TCF7 expression on tumors and CD39 blockade correspond to ICB efficacy in melanoma patients.
source: Using scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and TCR-seq to query ICB responsiveness in melanoma patients revealed a variety of T cell-related factors that correspond to ICB efficacy including TCF7 expression on tumors and CD39 blockade (Sade-Feldman et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sade-Feldman et al., 2018.

claim: The lung cancer TME is enriched for T cells that are dysfunctional or regulatory.
source: In agreement with scRNA-seq reports, a mass cytometry approach found that the lung cancer TME is enriched for T cells that are dysfunctional or regulatory (Lavin et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lavin et al., 2017.

claim: B cells can elicit immunosuppressive activity through expression of PD-L1 and production of IL-10, IL-35, and TGF-β.
source: Some B cells can elicit immunosuppressive activity, including in the context of malignancy, through a variety of mechanisms including expression of PD-L1 and production of IL-10, IL-35, and TGF-β leading some to refer to this subset as regulatory B cells (Bregs) in analogy to Tregs (Schioppa et al., 2011; Yanaba et al., 2008; Rosser and Mauri, 2015; DiLillo et al., 2010; Khan et al., 2015; Olkhanud et al., 2011; Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schioppa et al., 2011; Yanaba et al., 2008; Rosser and Mauri, 2015; DiLillo et al., 2010; Khan et al., 2015; Olkhanud et al., 2011; and Huang et al., 2017.

claim: B cells can promote lymphangiogenesis.
source: Furthermore, B cells can promote lymphangiogenesis (Angeli et al., 2006), which, in turn, can enable trafficking of DCs or tumor cells themselves from primary tumors to draining LNs (Roberts et al., 2016; Binnewies et al., 2019; Stacker et al., 2014; Tammela and Alitalo, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Angeli et al., 2006.

claim: The presence and differentiation of B cells within GCs correlates with improved prognosis.
source: Like SLOs, these TLSs contain germinal centers (GCs) where B cells can proliferate and undergo class switching and somatic hypermutation (GeurtsvanKessel et al., 2009; Perros et al., 2012; Neyt et al., 2012), and the presence and differentiation of B cells, in particular, within GCs correlates with improved prognosis (Germain et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Germain et al., 2014.

claim: Activation of humoral responses within TLS can improve responses, particularly in the context of immunotherapy.
source: Thus, activation of humoral responses within TLS can improve responses, particularly in the context of immunotherapy (Germain et al., 2014; Helmink et al., 2020; Montfort et al., 2017; Sautès-Fridman et al., 2016; Cottrell et al., 2018; Sautès-Fridman et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Germain et al., 2014; Helmink et al., 2020; Montfort et al., 2017; Sautès-Fridman et al., 2016; Cottrell et al., 2018; and Sautès-Fridman et al., 2019.

claim: Combining tumor-binding antibodies with DC adjuvants and CD40 agonists results in extremely potent anti-tumor responses in a manner that is FcR-dependent.
source: Furthermore, while FcR binding of tumor-immune complexes has been suggested to promote tumor progression (Andreu et al., 2010), we have found that combining tumor-binding antibodies with DC adjuvants and CD40 agonists results in extremely potent anti-tumor responses in a manner that is FcR-dependent (Spitzer et al., 2017; Carmi et al., 2015; Carmi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Spitzer et al., 2017; Carmi et al., 2015; and Carmi et al., 2016.

claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of melanoma and RCC responders and non-responders revealed a strong enrichment in B cell signatures in responders.
source: To understand the role of TLS B cells during immunotherapy, one group combined bulk RNA-seq of melanoma and renal cell carcinoma (RCC) responders and non-responders with deconvolution algorithms to identify a strong enrichment in B cell signatures in responders.
evidence: This is based on data from RNA-seq analysis of patient samples.

claim: ICB responders showed increases in both clonal diversity and expansion of individual BCR clones.
source: They further analyzed the BCRs of these patients from the bulk RNA-seq and found increases in both clonal diversity and expansion of individual clones in responders, suggesting antigen-specific humoral responses.
evidence: This is based on BCR sequencing data from patient samples.

claim: Mass cytometry demonstrated an enrichment for memory B cells, plasma cells, and GC B cells specifically within the tumors of ICB responders.
source: Finally, using mass cytometry, they demonstrated an enrichment for memory B cells, plasma cells, and GC B cells specifically within the tumors of responders, suggesting a role for B cell activation and humoral responses in patients benefiting from ICB (Helmink et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Helmink et al., 2020.

claim: The prognosis of patients often strongly correlates with the degree of T cell infiltration into the local tumor microenvironment (TME).
source: Studies investigating the immune status of tumors have revealed that the prognosis of patients often strongly correlates with the degree of T cell infiltration into the local tumor microenvironment (TME) (Galon et al., 2006; Binnewies et al., 2018; Gajewski et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Galon et al., 2006; Binnewies et al., 2018; and Gajewski et al., 2013.

claim: Immune infiltrates have served as effective prognostic biomarkers of response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB).
source: Immune infiltrates have also served as effective prognostic biomarkers of response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) (Herbst et al., 2014; Tumeh et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Herbst et al., 2014 and Tumeh et al., 2014.

claim: Lymph node metastases can render the systemic immune response permissive to tumor progression.
source: Further studies are needed to comprehensively interrogate systemic immune responses to metastases, as lymph node metastases can render the systemic immune response permissive to tumor progression (Reticker-Flynn et al., 2020), and the invocation of systemic immunity is required for the efficacy of immunotherapy (Spitzer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Reticker-Flynn et al., 2020.

claim: The invocation of systemic immunity is required for the efficacy of immunotherapy.
source: Further studies are needed to comprehensively interrogate systemic immune responses to metastases, as lymph node metastases can render the systemic immune response permissive to tumor progression (Reticker-Flynn et al., 2020), and the invocation of systemic immunity is required for the efficacy of immunotherapy (Spitzer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Spitzer et al., 2017.

claim: In order for a given mutation to result in T cell recognition, it must be in a protein coding region, be non-synonymous, be in a gene that is expressed by the tumor cells, be maintained following proteasomal degradation, result in a peptide that can be loaded onto the specific MHC-I molecules of that patient, and be recognized by the TCR of a T cell that can enter the tumor.
source: In order for a given mutation to result in T cell recognition, it must be in a protein coding region, be non-synonymous, be in a gene that is expressed by the tumor cells, be maintained following proteasomal degradation, result in a peptide that can be loaded onto the specific MHC-I molecules of that patient, and, of course, be recognized by the TCR of a T cell that can enter the tumor.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of antigen presentation and T cell recognition.

claim: Efficacy of ICB is correlated with neoantigen burden for a variety of cancers.
source: Furthermore, efficacy of ICB is correlated with neoantigen burden for a variety of cancers (Yarchoan et al., 2017; Snyder et al., 2014; Carbone et al., 2017; Rizvi et al., 2015a; Galsky et al., 2017; McGranahan et al., 2016), and tumor mutational burden (TMB) may be a better predictor of ICB response than PD-L1-positive staining in some instances (Hellmann et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yarchoan et al., 2017; Snyder et al., 2014; Carbone et al., 2017; Rizvi et al., 2015a; Galsky et al., 2017; and McGranahan et al., 2016.

claim: Tumor mutational burden (TMB) may be a better predictor of ICB response than PD-L1-positive staining in some instances.
source: Furthermore, efficacy of ICB is correlated with neoantigen burden for a variety of cancers (Yarchoan et al., 2017; Snyder et al., 2014; Carbone et al., 2017; Rizvi et al., 2015a; Galsky et al., 2017; McGranahan et al., 2016), and tumor mutational burden (TMB) may be a better predictor of ICB response than PD-L1-positive staining in some instances (Hellmann et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hellmann et al., 2018.

claim: The degree to which neoantigens are shared across tumor clones correlates with ICB efficacy.
source: Furthermore, the degree to which neoantigens are shared across tumor clones also correlates with ICB efficacy (McGranahan et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to McGranahan et al., 2016.

claim: A neural network algorithm trained on LC-MS/MS data of peptides eluted from single HLA allele-expressing cell lines predicted peptide loading with a higher degree of accuracy than preexisting binding affinity-based approaches.
source: To improve HLA-binding prediction, the same researchers used an LC-MS/MS approach wherein peptides were eluted from single HLA allele-expressing cell lines and subjected to MS resulting in the identification of 24,000 peptides and their cognate HLA class I molecules (Abelin et al., 2017). Furthermore, using this database of peptide-MHC interactions, they trained a neural network algorithm to predict peptide loading with a higher degree of accuracy than preexisting binding affinity-based approaches.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Abelin et al., 2017.

claim: Initial neoantigen vaccine trials have been extended to glioblastoma and appear to generate antigen-specific T cells and increases in tumor infiltration by the T cells.
source: The initial neoantigen vaccine trials have now been extended to glioblastoma, a notoriously immune cold tumor, and appear to generate antigen-specific T cells and increases in tumor infiltration by the T cells (Keskin et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Keskin et al., 2019.

claim: A given TCR is capable of recognizing hundreds of distinct peptides provided that they contain specific 'hot spots' where the TCR contacts the complex.
source: One elegant systems-level study used yeast display of peptide-MHC constructs to reveal that a given TCR is capable of recognizing hundreds of distinct peptides provided that they contain specific 'hot spots' where the TCR contacts the complex (Birnbaum et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Birnbaum et al., 2014.

claim: GLIPH is an algorithm capable of grouping TCRs based on predicted shared epitopes using similarity of the CDR3 regions.
source: To address this need, researchers developed GLIPH, an algorithm capable of grouping TCRs based on predicted shared epitopes using similarity of the CDR3 regions and demonstrated that they could predict shared binding partners across individuals (Glanville et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Glanville et al., 2017.

claim: TCRdist is an algorithm that groups TCRs of related specificities.
source: Another study combined MHC tetramer selection with single-cell TCR sequencing to develop an algorithm, TCRdist, that also groups TCRs of related specificities (Dash et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dash et al., 2017.

claim: Exhausted and effector CD8+ T cells in tumors shared clonotypes with memory T cells but not with each other.
source: By comparing clonotypes with phenotypes, they showed that exhausted and effector CD8+ T cells in tumors shared clonotypes with memory T cells but not with each other, suggesting that these distinct states are not shared between the same T cell clones.
evidence: This is based on data from single-cell TCR and RNA sequencing of patient samples.

claim: Anti-PD1 treatment resulted in considerable expansion of TEx that did not exist before therapy, with only minor contributions from pre-existing TCF7+ clones.
source: Even more notably, they found considerable expansion of TEx post-treatment that did not exist before therapy, with only minor contributions from pre-existing TCF7+ clones.
evidence: This is based on data from single-cell TCR and RNA sequencing of patient samples before and after ICB.

claim: Anti-PD1 stimulates recruitment of new tumor-specific T cells to the TME.
source: In contrast with conventional wisdom suggesting that ICB works by reinvigorating existing T cells within the TME, these results suggest that anti-PD1 stimulates recruitment of new tumor-specific T cells to the TME and are in agreement with our own findings that trafficking of lymphocytes from SLOs is required for effective immunotherapy (Spitzer et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing expansion of new clones and is supported by a citation to Spitzer et al., 2017.

claim: Trafficking of lymphocytes from SLOs is required for effective immunotherapy.
source: In contrast with conventional wisdom suggesting that ICB works by reinvigorating existing T cells within the TME, these results suggest that anti-PD1 stimulates recruitment of new tumor-specific T cells to the TME and are in agreement with our own findings that trafficking of lymphocytes from SLOs is required for effective immunotherapy (Spitzer et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Spitzer et al., 2017.

claim: TIL therapy has proven effective, and even curative, in a number of malignancies including melanoma, breast cancer, and multiple GI cancers.
source: It is important to note that autologous transplant of ex vivo expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL therapy) has proven effective, and even curative, in a number of malignancies including melanoma, breast cancer, and multiple GI cancers (Rosenberg et al., 1988; Rosenberg and Restifo, 2015; Dudley et al., 2002; Restifo et al., 2012; Tran et al., 2014; Tran et al., 2016; Zacharakis et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rosenberg et al., 1988; Rosenberg and Restifo, 2015; Dudley et al., 2002; Restifo et al., 2012; Tran et al., 2014; Tran et al., 2016; and Zacharakis et al., 2018.

claim: Some melanoma patients who have failed ICB still benefit from TIL therapy.
source: Moreover, in the case of melanoma, some patients who have failed ICB still benefit from TIL therapy (Sarnaik et al., 2020; Rohaan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sarnaik et al., 2020 and Rohaan et al., 2018.

claim: The microbiome affects everything from obesity, to resistance to colonization by pathogenic bacteria, to cancer.
source: The microbiome affects everything from obesity, to resistance to colonization by pathogenic bacteria, to cancer (Ridaura et al., 2013; Petersen et al., 2019; Jacobson et al., 2018; Iida et al., 2013; Buffie et al., 2015; van Nood et al., 2013; Viaud et al., 2013; Sivan et al., 2015; Vetizou et al., 2015; Gopalakrishnan et al., 2018; Routy et al., 2018; Tanoue et al., 2019; Matson et al., 2018; Garrett, 2015; Reticker-Flynn and Engleman, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Specific commensal consortia are capable of inducing expansion of Tregs.
source: Through 16S rRNA sequencing of the caecal contents of mice exhibiting enrichment of particular T cell subsets in their colons following fecal transplant or in comparison to mice under different housing conditions, they were able to define commensal consortia capable of inducing expansion of Tregs (Atarashi et al., 2013), TH1 (Atarashi et al., 2017), TH17 (Ivanov et al., 2009; Gaboriau-Routhiau et al., 2009), or IFN-γ+ CD8+ T cells (Tanoue et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Atarashi et al., 2013.

claim: Specific commensal consortia are capable of inducing expansion of TH1 cells.
source: Through 16S rRNA sequencing of the caecal contents of mice exhibiting enrichment of particular T cell subsets in their colons following fecal transplant or in comparison to mice under different housing conditions, they were able to define commensal consortia capable of inducing expansion of Tregs (Atarashi et al., 2013), TH1 (Atarashi et al., 2017), TH17 (Ivanov et al., 2009; Gaboriau-Routhiau et al., 2009), or IFN-γ+ CD8+ T cells (Tanoue et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Atarashi et al., 2017.

claim: Specific commensal consortia are capable of inducing expansion of TH17 cells.
source: Through 16S rRNA sequencing of the caecal contents of mice exhibiting enrichment of particular T cell subsets in their colons following fecal transplant or in comparison to mice under different housing conditions, they were able to define commensal consortia capable of inducing expansion of Tregs (Atarashi et al., 2013), TH1 (Atarashi et al., 2017), TH17 (Ivanov et al., 2009; Gaboriau-Routhiau et al., 2009), or IFN-γ+ CD8+ T cells (Tanoue et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Ivanov et al., 2009 and Gaboriau-Routhiau et al., 2009.

claim: Specific commensal consortia are capable of inducing expansion of IFN-γ+ CD8+ T cells.
source: Through 16S rRNA sequencing of the caecal contents of mice exhibiting enrichment of particular T cell subsets in their colons following fecal transplant or in comparison to mice under different housing conditions, they were able to define commensal consortia capable of inducing expansion of Tregs (Atarashi et al., 2013), TH1 (Atarashi et al., 2017), TH17 (Ivanov et al., 2009; Gaboriau-Routhiau et al., 2009), or IFN-γ+ CD8+ T cells (Tanoue et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tanoue et al., 2019.

claim: Bifidobacterium aids anti-PD-1 therapy in mice.
source: Moreover, specific commensals affected responses to ICB, with Bifidobacterium aiding anti-PD-1 (Sivan et al., 2015) and Bacteroidales fragilis aiding anti-CTLA-4 (Vetizou et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sivan et al., 2015.

claim: Bacteroidales fragilis aids anti-CTLA-4 therapy in mice.
source: Moreover, specific commensals affected responses to ICB, with Bifidobacterium aiding anti-PD-1 (Sivan et al., 2015) and Bacteroidales fragilis aiding anti-CTLA-4 (Vetizou et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vetizou et al., 2015.

claim: Increased diversity and enrichment for Ruminococcaceae family bacteria correlate with improved response to anti-PD-1 and increases in CD8+ T cell activity in humans.
source: These results showed that increased diversity and enrichment for Ruminococcaceae family bacteria correlate with improved response to anti-PD-1 and increases in CD8+ T cell activity (Gopalakrishnan et al., 2018) and that Bifidobacterium longum, Collinsella aerofaciens, and Enterococcus faecium may also augment responses by expanding tumor-specific CD8+ T cells without affecting Treg numbers (Matson et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gopalakrishnan et al., 2018.

claim: Bifidobacterium longum, Collinsella aerofaciens, and Enterococcus faecium may augment responses to anti-PD-1 by expanding tumor-specific CD8+ T cells without affecting Treg numbers.
source: These results showed that increased diversity and enrichment for Ruminococcaceae family bacteria correlate with improved response to anti-PD-1 and increases in CD8+ T cell activity (Gopalakrishnan et al., 2018) and that Bifidobacterium longum, Collinsella aerofaciens, and Enterococcus faecium may also augment responses by expanding tumor-specific CD8+ T cells without affecting Treg numbers (Matson et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Matson et al., 2018.

claim: Fecal transplant into mice from human ICB responders resulted in increased efficacy of PD-1 blockade compared to that from non-responders.
source: Similarly, fecal transplant into mice from human ICB responders resulted in increased efficacy of PD-1 blockade compared to that from non-responders, possibly due to the effects on recruitment of a CD4+ T cell subset (Routy et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Routy et al., 2018.

claim: Evaluation of neoantigen burden by WES has revealed that the response to anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD1 therapies correlates with mutational burden.
source: In addition to the utility of WES in vaccine design, evaluation of neoantigen burden by WES has revealed that the response to anti-CTLA-4 (Snyder et al., 2014) and anti-PD1 (Rizvi et al., 2015a) therapies correlates with mutational burden.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Snyder et al., 2014 and Rizvi et al., 2015a.

claim: Mass cytometry identified differences in lymphocyte populations and evidence of classical monocyte activation in PBMCs of patients who responded to anti-PD1.
source: One study identified not only differences in lymphocyte populations but also evidence of classical monocyte activation in PBMCs of patients who responded to anti-PD1 (Krieg et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Krieg et al., 2018.

claim: The key differentiator of effective immune responses is its orchestration from extratumoral sites such as LNs rather than a simple reinvigoration of existing TILs.
source: In addition to identifying differences in key immune populations such as a subset activated memory CD4+ T cells, we found that the key differentiator of effective immune responses is its orchestration from extratumoral sites such as LNs rather than a simple reinvigoration of existing TILs.
evidence: This is based on data from organism-wide mass cytometry analysis.

claim: Cancer immunotherapy, and ICB in particular, represents one of the most significant advances in oncology in decades and has the ability to elicit durable responses and cures in some patients with advanced stage malignancies.
source: Cancer immunotherapy, and ICB in particular, represents one of the most significant advances in oncology in decades and has the ability to elicit durable responses and cures in some patients with advanced stage malignancies (Rosenberg and Restifo, 2015; Brahmer et al., 2012; Hamid et al., 2013; Hodi et al., 2010; Nghiem et al., 2016; Pardoll, 2012; Robert et al., 2015; Sharma and Allison, 2015; Rizvi et al., 2015b; Grupp et al., 2013; Brentjens et al., 2013; Porter et al., 2011; June et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The majority of patients who receive ICB therapy do not exhibit durable responses.
source: Nonetheless, while subsets of patients with melanoma, RCC, Hodgkin's lymphoma, NSCLC, urothelial cancer, and MSI high GI cancers have experienced durable responses and even complete tumor regression (Zappasodi et al., 2018), the majority of patients who receive the therapy do not exhibit such responses.
evidence: This is inferred from the statement that only subsets of patients respond, implying the majority do not.
